title: helm(private): stabilize values schema v2 + init-hook/upgrade rollback fixes
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: private installer (Helm) churn during upgrades caused repeated init-hook failures and schema regressions for values.yaml. This PR stabilizes the values.schema.json (v2), tightens templating defaults, and hardens the init/upgrade/rollback hooks so upgrades are resilient across minor chart and K8s changes.

Summary of changes: - Promote values.schema.json to v2 with explicit validations for encryption, nodeAffinity, tolerations, and KMS config. - Add deterministic defaults for PVC templating and consistent labels/annotations to avoid spurious diffs during chart upgrades. - Refactor init-hook to be idempotent: use job backoffLimits, pre-checks for PV existence, and a reconciliation-style marker ConfigMap so retries are safe. - Add a dedicated upgrade-job that runs logical pre/post steps (migrations, secret re-writes) and supports a --dry-run via Helm values. - Add compatibility mappings for older release values (compatibility shim) so rolling upgrades from 1.x chart versions do not error out on strict schema.

Checklist: - [x] values.schema.json v2 added and tested against sample values files - [x] init-hook idempotency and backoff limits implemented - [x] upgrade-job added and integrated with helm hooks - [x] compatibility shim for legacy values - [x] unit + integration tests for installer flows - [x] docs updated (charts/redwood-private/README.md)

Testing/verification: See testing_notes below for CI runs and local validation steps. Also validated upgrade path from v1.13.2 -> this branch on a local kind cluster and on a staging GKE cluster used by the private installer e2e suite.

Related: linear ENG-1723 (private-installer upgrade stability), ENG-1831 (helm values schema cleanup). Jira SUP-4421 contains a customer incident where an upgrade failed due to missing tolerations validation.

Notes: kept the description concise; see commit messages for granular context and file diffs for exact templating changes.

review_threads: Diego Morales: Please add a comment on why we chose a ConfigMap marker rather than an annotation. (commented 2025-11-06)

Ava Chen: ConfigMap chosen because annotations on Jobs can be dropped by k8s controllers during retries; ConfigMap gives a stable cluster-scoped object we can check across retries. Updated PR with rationale. (reply 2025-11-06)
Ethan Brooks: CI failed on integration-private-installer the first run (timeout on e2e upgrade). Looks like the upgrade-job needs a higher backoff limit. (commented 2025-11-08)
Ava Chen: Increased backoffLimit to 6 and added readiness pre-check to skip if markers already present. Reran CI. (reply 2025-11-09)
Priya Nair: Left a nit on values.schema.json around optional vs required KMS fields - prefer explicit required list for HSM customers. (commented 2025-11-10)
Ava Chen: tightened required fields to only require kms.type when encryption.enabled is true - added conditional schema rule and test. (reply 2025-11-11)
Priya Nair: Approving after tests green. (approved 2025-11-19)

integration-tests/private-installer: flaky -> rerun -> pass (e2e upgrade, timeout handled by increased backoffLimit)
testing_notes: Local verification steps: 1) helm dependency update && helm template charts/redwood-private --values samples/values-legacy.yaml --validate (should apply compat shim) 2) Deploy to kind cluster, run charts/redwood-private/templates/init-hook-job.yaml and ensure marker ConfigMap created and retry-safe 3) Run upgrade-job with dry-run flag and verify migrations do not mutate secrets unexpectedly. CI runs include integration-private-installer and e2e/upgrade-rollback which were used to validate staging GKE path.

changelog_entry: redwood-private: values.schema v2, idempotent init hooks, upgrade-job and compat shim (PR #51234)
notes_for_ops: When performing manual upgrades, set 'upgrade.dryRun=true' first to validate migration steps. If a job fails, ensure the marker ConfigMap is absent or review logs from secret-rewrite-job. For customers using HSM/KMS, validate kms.type and kms.keyArn are present when encryption.enabled=true.
